variants.prompt: Use case scientific-educational. Wide horizontal 3:1 panoramic miniature geological drilling exhibition on one ivory unrolled paper scroll, curled wooden ends fully visible. Modern museum craft, paper and matte stone, soft neutral studio daylight, restrained cinnabar-red drilling equipment, blue-gray, natural ochre, offwhite. FOUR distinct coherent left-to-right physical zones: (1) a cutaway layered geological rock block with a modest red drill rig and a drillstring tilted slightly along the borehole, no oil reservoirs or pipelines; (2) a clearly separate compact driller control console with pressure/rotary controls without markings and drillbit/collar components on a small bench; (3) a field measurement desk with closed logger, blank long vertical paper strips and blank open notebooks, monitor screen OFF; (4) several narrow vertical rock core stacks laid in an archival core tray beside blank depth-record cards and a red pencil. Different heights create spatial depth but balanced light detail, significant breathing room between zones. No texts, letters, numerals, fake data, curves, graphs, diagrams, arrow icons, numbered circles, gauges with numbers, neon or floating screens. Whole meaningful industrial/geological scene, not four icons. Not an oil refinery. Entire wide scroll fits frame.

Use case scientific-educational. A 3:1 horizontal warm ivory paper scroll unfolds as a modern museum diorama about recording drilling progress. Refined handcrafted miniature, tactile matte paper, naturally layered stone, subtle cinnabar red #B8242A and slate blue accents, neutral white gallery and gentle light. Four left-to-right spatial areas connected on same paper base, no enclosing boxes: left quarter a low geological cutaway block and red rig with slim drillstring going through layers; second area a visible rotary-drive assembly and clean WOB/control console with unmarked controls, small drill tools on bench; third area a tidy recording workstation with black OFF screen, logger and several long entirely BLANK vertical paper ribbons hanging over a desk edge; right quarter a wide open field record book with blank divider tabs, sealed sample boxes and a second narrow geological section block made of several clearly different rock textures, not colored toy cubes. Slight isometric viewpoint with enough depth to feel solid, restrained visual density. Do not put graphs, curves, waveforms, arrows, number ticks, letters, text, labels, badges, neon screens or people anywhere. Full scroll ends fit frame. Designed as macro navigation artwork, not a measured scientific diagram; no unrelated refinery or futuristic facilities.
